# FDG9162

> DO use the prefix “Try” and a Boolean return type for methods implementing the Try-Write Pattern.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.12.3 Writing Values to Buffers with the Try-Write Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9162
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Give the Try-Write method '{0}' the prefix Try and a Boolean return type

The text has no body; the body of FDG9165 and the introduction of section 9.12.3 describe the pattern. FDG9162 reports an externally visible method with a parameter named destination of type Span<T>, Memory<T>, an array or ArraySegment<T> and an out parameter of an integer type whose name ends with Written, the shape of the Try-Write Pattern, when it returns bool but its name does not start with Try followed by an uppercase letter, or when its name starts so but it does not return bool. A method that returns OperationStatus has the same parameters in the pattern of section 9.12.4 and is not reported. Try-Write methods with other parameter names, overrides and interface implementations are not seen, so coverage is partial. Renaming or changing the return type changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.
